chapter: Bix, Trumbauer and the Goldkette sidemen
title: Bix Beiderbecke as the jazz outlet of the band
summary: Morehouse says Bix came in at the same time he did, was quiet, inspired everyone and never played a solo the same way twice.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Let me ask you, I know you've been asked this question before. Tell me about Bix. What was he like?
Bix Beiderbecke.
Bix Beiderbecke, tell me about Bix. What do you remember of him?
Well Bix came into the band as I came into the band.
About the same time?
Yeah.
Okay.
And he was the jazz outlet for the whole band.
What do you mean by that?
I mean he played jazz.
He was the way the band...
He stimulated everybody.
Okay, that's what I mean. He led the way toward the jazz feeling.
That's right, that's right.
And what kind of a guy was he? Did you know him well?
He was a fine guy, yeah.
Quiet?
Yeah, quiet. Sometimes he would get up under the...
Bandstand, Chauncey? Bandstand.
Yeah, the bandstand.
What would he do?
And tip his hat and go on and finally find his way back into the band.
You mean he would just walk away from the bandstand.
Yeah.
I don't understand. Why would he do that?
Well he had certain things that the other people in the band had.
How did Bix play, darling.
What?
Explain. Terrific horn. He inspired everybody.
Right. The other members of the band knew that he was a genius.
Sure.
It wasn't that 50 years later...or anything
No, no.
It was true of Bix. And everybody would just be so keyed up, because he just seemed to be his inspiration.
Uh huh.
And they all jammed like mad. And everybody followed him. And that's how Bix played too. And he didn't play the same thing twice.
No sir, never played the same thing twice.
And he didn't play....
Isn't that because he couldn't read the music too well and he had to improvise.
He was improvising all the time. The same song might be different every time he played it. He was so great on that horn.
